title: soft-quota tranche allocator and high-fidelity utilization reporter
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets need a predictable, low-friction way to offer short-term capacity above tenant commitments without hard preemption. This PR introduces a soft-quota tranche allocator (SQTA) that slices a tenant's burst entitlement into time-boxed tranches that can be borrowed and gradually reclaimed with graceful degradation. Complementing SQTA is a high-fidelity utilization reporter (HFUR) that provides minute-resolution occupancy histograms, GPU slot-level tail metrics, and correlation signals for latency/throughput regressions.

Design summary: SQTA implements per-tenant 'tranche windows' (configurable size and decay). Each tranche is an ephemeral allowance consumed from a soft pool; consumption updates a credit ledger with linear decay + emergency drain. Reclamation uses a prioritized drain policy: first reclaim idle tranches, then slow-start backoff on warm clients, finally gentle evictions based on age and SLA tier. HFUR samples per-GPU occupancy and KV-cache hotness at 60s granularity, exports percentile series (p50/p90/p99) and an occupancy histogram (8 buckets) to Prometheus and the telemetry pipeline. A new sampling agent runs on dedicated nodes to avoid control-plane pressure.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (link to Linear ENG-7421) - [x] Unit tests for ledger arithmetic and decay - [x] E2E smoke in perf-canary - [x] Backwards compatibility tests (old allocators ignored when SQTA disabled) - [x] Migration script for existing soft pools

Commits summary: squash of feature work + fixes (see commit_list). Key changes: new allocator service, ledger protobufs, tranche admission controller, sampling agent + exporter, metrics dashboards, and CLI flags.

Files touched (high level): allocator/ (implementation + tests), runtime/ledger/ (protobuf + persistence shim), telemetry/sampler/ (agent + exporter), dashboards/sqta-overview.json, docs/architecture/sqta.md, infra/deploy/ (helm values + feature flag).

Behavioral notes: - SQTA is behind a feature flag (sqta.enabled=false by default) to allow staged rollout. - Tranche borrow is metered and surfaced on tenant billing UI via new per-tranche consumption metric. - HFUR adds a small (~0.6% CPU) overhead on dedicated nodes; perf-canary validated no regression in median latency for typical workloads.

Testing & CI: unit + integration + perf-canary stable; CI intermittently failed on lint initially and was fixed in follow-up commit. All pipelines green on merge.

Backward compatibility and migration: migration script migrates soft-pool entries to tranche-indexed ledger; schema version bump included. If migration fails, feature flag can be toggled off and system will fallback to legacy soft pool behavior.

Related: follows work in ENG-6122 (soft pools), complements autoscaler improvements in PRs that introduce headroom smoothing.

Merge: squashed and merged to main after approvals from Priya and Diego. Rollout plan: enable sqta for 10% of dedicated fleets for 48h, monitor HFUR signals and SLOs, then progressive ramp to 100% over 7 days.

release_notes: Introduce soft-quota tranches (SQTA) for safer burst capacity and add high-fidelity utilization reporting. SQTA is behind a feature flag and will be rolled out gradually. New metrics: tenant_tranche_consumption, gpu_occupancy_histogram, gpu_slot_tail_latency_p99.
